correctness.rationale: Explicit ε<min[1/(2(1+cd)),1/(2d),1/(2(1+d))] makes the positive rectangle invariant. For r=x/y and T=1/y, exact recurrences r_next−r = r*y[(1−c)−(1+d)r]/(1−y+dx), T_next−T=(1−dr)/(1−y+dx). x decreases by logistic comparison; y→0 by eventually weak predator forcing, but y_next≥y(1−y) implies Σy diverges. For c<1, r contracts toward r*=(1−c)/(1+d), yielding both n limits. For c≥1, r→0 and T/n→1. For c>1 a polynomial upper bound for r makes Σx finite and Σ|y−1/n| finite; log x_n+c log n converges, yielding L>0. For c=1 exact w=y/x satisfies w_next−w=(1+d)y/(1−x−y). First w~(1+d)log n, then reciprocal T=n−[d/(1+d)]n/log n+O(n loglog n/log² n), and the resulting summable difference correction gives w−(1+d)log n−d loglog n→C.
